content.title: About
content.content: Spanish rice is a long‑grain variety traditionally used in Spanish cuisine, especially in paella. It has a subtle aromatic flavor, absorbs sauces well, and holds its shape during cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The rice used for paella is often called “balsa” and is cultivated in the Valencia and Catalonia regions.
Traditional paella preparation avoids stirring the rice so that a crust called “socarrat” forms at the bottom.
Spanish rice has a higher amylopectin content, making it slightly stickier than ordinary long‑grain rice.
In Spain, rice is considered a key part of the national culinary heritage and is protected by a geographical indication.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Rice provides sustained energy through slowly digestible carbs.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: It contains less than 1 g of fat per 100 g, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: It supplies thiamine, niacin, and vitamin B6, which support metabolism.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Rice provides magnesium and phosphorus, important for muscle and bone health.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Rice can raise blood sugar quickly, so people with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Arsenic in raw grains
items.content: Some rice varieties may contain trace arsenic; choose reputable brands and rinse well before cooking.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Spanish rice is perfect for paella, risotto, salads, and side dishes. Cook it in broth, add vegetables, seafood or meat. Rinse the rice before cooking to remove excess starch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store rice in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For long‑term storage, keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent pest infestation.
